'''Adriaan Vlacq''' (1600&ndash;1667) was a Dutch book publisher and author of mathematical tables.  Born in [[Gouda, South Holland|Gouda]], Vlacq published a table of  [[logarithms]] from 1 to 100,000 to 10 decimal places in 1628 in his ''[[Arithmetica logarithmica]]''. This table extended [[Henry Briggs (mathematician)|Henry Briggs']] original tables which only covered the values 1-20,000 and 90,001 to 100,000.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://locomat.loria.fr|title=LOCOMAT: The LORIA COLLECTION of MATHEMATICAL TABLES|work=loria.fr}}</ref> The new table was computed by [[Ezechiel de Decker]] and Vlacq who calculated and added 70,000 further values to complete the tables. This table was further extended by [[Jurij Vega]] in 1794, and by [[Alexander John Thompson]] in 1952.

A shorter trigonometric table called '''''Canon Sinuum''''' was included in later works of Vlacq.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=omUVAAAAQAAJ&pg=PA49 |title=Tables de sinus, tangentes, secantes et de logarithmes des sinus, tangentes ... - Adriaan Vlacq - Google Livres |access-date=2016-04-15|last1=Vlacq |first1=Adriaan |year=1651 }}</ref>

In 1632, he settled in [[London]] but ten years later with the onset of the [[English Civil War]], he moved to [[Paris]] and later moved to [[The Hague]].{{fact|date=June 2024}}

He died at The Hague on 8 April 1667.{{fact|date=June 2024}}

The crater [[Vlacq (crater)|Vlacq]] on the Moon is named after him.<ref>https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/6420</ref>
